name: RB-Dustv2 and DaN-Dust
description: Autonomous agricultural machines must be able to operate during the day and at night and simultaneously cope with dust raised during soil cultivation. Dust can obscure a vehicle’s perception and restrict the farmer’s view when operating the machine. This study presents the data and the evaluation procedures for developing and comparing methods for removing dust generated during tillage from camera images. To this end, we developed a benchmark consisting of two datasets: RB-Dustv2 and DaN-Dust. These datasets can be used for developing and refining dust removal methods. The DaN-Dust dataset contains unpaired dusty and dust-free images recorded during tillage with a disc harrow, both during the day and at night. The DaN-Dust dataset includes 1,042 training image sets, each containing one dusty image and one dust-free image, as well as 105 individual dusty images for testing. Additionally, we present the RB-Dustv2 dataset, which contains 50 training sets and 10 testing sets of paired dusty and dust-free images. We benchmarked state-of-the-art image dehazing, image translation, image restoration, and image dedusting methods using the proposed datasets. Specifically, we selected prior-guided, supervised, and unsupervised approaches. A comprehensive evaluation confirmed the usefulness of the presented datasets for researching and developing dust removal approaches.
